transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run 55 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Sara: Sara here, hi.
[00:10] Michael: Michael on infra.
[00:12] Jian: Jian, security.
[00:14] Tom: Tom, product.
[00:16] Liam: Liam from Redwood, SE.
[00:18] Noah: Noah, CSM.
[00:20] Ava: Great. Agenda: quick results recap, canary plan, monitoring & runbooks, cutover dates.
[00:30] Sara: Quick note — pilot has been good, latency medians around 180ms for our 1k token average, tails hit 600ms sometimes, cost is within ballpark but we want to reduce the 95th percentile.
[00:45] Liam: Right, the 95th tail looks related to some batch sizes and KV cache misses on longer context. We're seeing tokenization spikes when prefix cache invalidates. We recommended prefix pre-warming and a 2s batching window in earlier notes.
[01:05] Michael: If we pre-warm KV cache won't that increase memory? We're on a single dedicated pool for the POC. What's the tradeoff?
[01:20] Liam: Yes, slight memory bump but it reduces repeated encoder work and drops tail latency. We can tune batching to cap memory — also can disable cross-request caching for certain routes. We'll include configs in the runbook.
[01:35] Tom: On rollout options: product prefers a soft launch with A/B where 10% traffic on Redwood Dedicated and 90% stays on current infra. Security wants canary first then A/B. Thoughts?
[01:50] Ava: Typical flow we suggest is canary -> expand canary -> staged A/B. Canary gives us full-stack observability on real traffic small slice and rollback is simpler. A/B is good for feature validation but adds complexity to correlation.
[02:10] Sara: Okay canary sounds fine. How long should canary run? 24-72 hours?
[02:18] Liam: Depends on volume; for NovaHealth I'd recommend a 48 hour canary with SLOs monitored constantly and an automatic rollback if error rate or latency breach. We'll publish metric thresholds in the runbook.
[02:30] Jian: Security: we need audit logs, KMS integration for key management, SAML SSO group mappings and evidence for SOC 2 controls before full cutover. Can we get those docs?
[02:42] Ava: Yes, we'll share security pack — SOC 2, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration notes, and sample audit logs. Noah will attach the security deck.
[02:50] Noah: I'll share it after the call, also the checklist for on-prem and VPC setups.
[03:00] Michael: On networking, we need an IP allowlist and expected egress patterns for firewall rules. Also we prefer private endpoints; can Redwood support PrivateLink or equivalent?
[03:12] Liam: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink in the dedicated/private options — we'll include exact CIDR ranges and egress ports in the integration doc.
[03:24] Tom: Monitoring — what dashboards will you provide? We need request rate, latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token cost per route, and KV cache hit ratio.
[03:36] Liam: We'll provide a Grafana dashboard template plus managed dashboards in the Console. Metric names: request.latency_ms, request.errors, model.token_count, cache.kv_hit_rate. We'll add SLO alerts for latency and error rate.
[03:50] Sara: Also want user-facing degradation behavior — graceful fallback to smaller model if latency breaches. Is automatic fallback supported?
[03:58] Liam: Yes we have routing policies — latency-based fallback to smaller quantized variant, and can do region fallback too. We'll include policies in runbook.
[04:10] Michael: For A/B we need deterministic routing so we can correlate user IDs. Any SDK support?
[04:18] Liam: Yes, SDK supports sticky routing keys and headers to route consistent user buckets. We can demonstrate in a short dev demo.
[04:30] Ava: Benchmarks — we need a load test before canary. Liam, can you run with 10k qps pattern and a 95th latency target of <800ms?
[04:38] Liam: Yes, I'll spin up a benchmark with the same request mix and share results.
[04:42] Sara: About cutover timing — we're targeting the week of 2026-12-20 but we may want a weekday night window. Any blackout windows to be aware of?
[04:50] Ava: From Redwood side no major blackout; we prefer lower traffic windows. We'll coordinate on exact night.
[05:00] Jian: One more on compliance — KMS key rotation could be monthly per our policy. Will Redwood respect customer-managed keys and rotation schedule?
[05:08] Liam: We support customer-managed keys (CMK) and we can surface rotation events and key IDs in audit logs. We'll document rotation process.
[05:18] Tom: What about cost during canary? Will billing show per-route token breakdown?
[05:24] Noah: Console provides token-level cost per route and per token type, yes — we'll share a sample report.
[05:32] Sara: I also want the rollback plan. If we see a 3x error spike, how fast is rollback?
[05:40] Ava: We have automatic rollback triggers you can set — immediate rollback on breaches or manual rollback which is a button in Console. Typically rollback completes within 2-5 minutes depending on DNS propagation and routing filters.
[05:52] Michael: For the runbook, can we have a checklist: pre-cutover smoke tests, canary ramp schedule, rollback steps, stakeholder contact list?
[06:00] Liam: Yep — the runbook will have pre-checks, canary ramp (10% -> 30% -> 60% over 48hrs), monitoring thresholds, rollback commands and contacts.
[06:12] Sara: Great. Anything about data residency? We need EU region for some workloads.
[06:18] Ava: We can pin region routing for sensitive routes — Dedicated can be kept in eu-west-1 and we'll ensure data doesn't leave region. We'll include region pinning config.
[06:28] Tom: Are there any outstanding blockers for go-live?
[06:32] Jian: Security sign-off and KMS confirmation.
[06:36] Michael: IP allowlist and test endpoints.
[06:40] Sara: Benchmarks from Redwood.
[06:42] Ava: Okay we'll own runbook, benchmarks, pricing, and security pack.
[06:48] Liam: I'll send the canary runbook draft by Friday (2026-12-11), run benchmarks by Monday (2026-12-14).
[06:56] Noah: I'll attach security docs and sample audit logs.
[07:02] Ava: Recap: share runbook, metrics dashboard, security pack, pricing. Next meeting to confirm cutover window once benchmarks and security items are complete.
[07:12] Sara: Thanks all.
[07:14] Tom: Thanks.
[07:16] Jian: Thanks.
[07:18] Ava: End.

Notes: transcript contains some transcription noise — occasional mis-attributions and small word errors typical of automated transcripts. Refer to attached runbook draft and security deck for authoritative details.
